A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic simulations, ImageNet/OpenOOD evaluations, covariance analyses, dimensionality experiments and preprocessing ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds CIFAR-10/100 evaluations and further analyses. These are distinct from the additional baseline scores explicitly attributed to the OpenOOD leaderboard.

M1.justification: The tied, full, diagonal and coupled-diagonal Gaussian DPMMs retain their priors, scoring procedures, EM estimation and numerical integration. The whitening/rotation procedure is also unchanged. New experimental configurations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 expands beyond synthetic data and ImageNet-1K to CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 as in-distribution tasks. Appendices K-L evaluate reciprocal CIFAR and Tiny ImageNet near-OOD scenarios, plus MNIST, Places365, SVHN and Textures far-OOD scenarios. The original coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds ASH and ReAct to the reported ImageNet comparison, and ASH, ReAct, SCALE and ReweightOOD to the CIFAR comparisons. These additional scores are explicitly sourced from the OpenOOD leaderboard, with ReweightOOD marked as an alternative training method. Independent RMDS, already evaluated on synthetic data in v1, additionally joins the real-data dimensionality comparison in Appendix M.

E3.justification: The added CIFAR experiments use pretrained 512-dimensional ResNet18 features, alongside the retained 768-dimensional ImageNet ViT features. V2 specifies covariance of class means for the tied model's CIFAR prior, versus data covariance for ImageNet, and evaluates raw versus whitened/rotated CIFAR features. These extend experimental settings; retained ImageNet protocols, synthetic settings and accuracy/AUROC metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4 and 6 extend preprocessing ablations to CIFAR, testing whether whitening/rotation benefits persist across datasets and features. Appendix M adds Independent RMDS to the ImageNet dimensionality sweep, directly testing independent covariance estimation against hierarchical sharing in high dimensions. The original ImageNet preprocessing ablation, synthetic sweeps and score-correlation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces parenthesized variability estimates throughout the CIFAR tables. Table 4 explicitly identifies standard deviations across three ResNet18 training runs with different seeds; Table 6 also reports parenthesized variability. V1 provides no corresponding seed or uncertainty reporting. This does not establish additional runs for the retained ImageNet results.

E6.justification: The original ImageNet results remain numerically unchanged in v2 Tables 2-3, including coupled-diagonal near-OOD AUROC 80.98 and tied-model far-OOD AUROC 92.70. New CIFAR-10 results give the full model 90.63/93.50 near/far AUROC versus RMDS 89.83/92.42 under W&R preprocessing. CIFAR-100 instead shows coupled-diagonal performance below RMDS. Added leaderboard entries and Figure 7's high-dimensional Independent RMDS collapse further expand the findings.

T1.justification: V1's heuristic Proposition 2 is replaced by Proposition 4.2 with explicit sub-Gaussian assumptions, a relative-covariance operator norm and a high-probability delta + log K bound. V2 adds an extended proof in Appendix E and computational complexity analysis in Appendix D. The proposition uses (C-d)/2, but the appendix conclusion inconsistently retains C/2-d.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: connecting RMDS to Bayesian nonparametric inference, introducing hierarchical covariance models including the coupled-diagonal model, and identifying regimes where these improve OOD detection. The additional evidence does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 shifts from emphasizing ImageNet near-OOD benefits to interpreting model suitability through dataset scale and complexity. Section 4 newly interprets the log K gap as aggregation across plausible clusters, and Appendix D discusses computational tradeoffs. The existing Gaussian-assumption and overfitting limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents the CIFAR feature source and dimensions, dataset-specific tied-model prior choices, typical convergence in about ten EM iterations, and the provenance and inherited classifier accuracies of leaderboard comparisons. Hardware, preprocessing instructions, EM initialization guidance and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting CIFAR/ResNet experiments, ASH, ReAct, SCALE, ReweightOOD and the expanded mathematical argument. Related work more explicitly states the post-hoc scope. The positioning relative to RMDS and earlier Bayesian nonparametric approaches remains stable; the author-year citation conversion is stylistic.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations and rewrites, renamed and expanded experimental appendices, revised cross-references, an added author and updated acknowledgments. These do not amount to a wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different journal layout and title/author presentation. Table 1 becomes a three-benchmark summary, while the original ImageNet table moves to Appendix J as Table 3. The revision expands comparison tables, adds CIFAR Tables 4-7, introduces a preprocessing flowchart and an additional dimensionality figure, and relabels the retained correlation plot.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis for judging when the models help. CIFAR/ResNet18 evaluations, preprocessing controls, seed variability and the real-data Independent RMDS comparison address v1's reliance on one real-data benchmark and backbone, revealing both benefits and failures. The explicit theoretical bound and cost discussion add useful specificity, although Appendix E's inconsistent constant scaling still requires correction. The broader, more diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net quality improvement.
